ucs.title: [LLM] TA505/Clop LEMURLOOT (human2.aspx) web shell drop on MOVEit Transfer
ucs.description: Hunts the TA505/Clop signature post-exploit artifact for CVE-2023-34362 — the IIS worker w3wp.exe writing the LEMURLOOT web shell (human2.aspx and variants) under the MOVEit Transfer wwwroot. This file-creation chain is the canonical IOC from CISA AA23-158A and is exclusive to this Clop/Indrik Spider campaign.
ucs.splunk: | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created AND Filesystem.process_name=w3wp.exe AND Filesystem.file_path="*\\MOVEitTransfer\\wwwroot\\*" AND (Filesystem.file_name=human2.aspx OR Filesystem.file_name=human.aspx OR Filesystem.file_name=_human2.aspx OR Filesystem.file_name=health.aspx) by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | where user!="*$"
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let WebShellNames = dynamic(["human2.aspx","human.aspx","_human2.aspx","health.aspx"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"                       // IIS worker — only the MOVEit web app should be writing aspx here
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\MOVEitTransfer\wwwroot\", @"\Progress\MOVEit Transfer\wwwroot\")
| where FileName in~ (WebShellNames)
     or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^human2?\.aspx?$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let WebShellNames = dynamic(["human2.aspx","human.aspx","_human2.aspx","health.aspx"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated"
| where ActingProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\MOVEitTransfer\wwwroot\", @"\Progress\MOVEit Transfer\wwwroot\")
| where TargetFileName in~ (WebShellNames)
     or TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^human2?\.aspx?$"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ucs.title: [LLM] TA505 Get2/SDBbot loader — Office → msiexec → rundll32 of user-writable DLL
ucs.description: Hunts TA505's signature initial-access chain: a weaponized Office document spawns msiexec.exe with a remote URL (downloading the Get2 MSI), which then invokes rundll32.exe against a DLL under AppData/ProgramData/Temp/Public (the SDBbot/FlawedAmmyy/ServHelper loader). The msiexec→rundll32 hand-off out of a user-writable directory under an Office grandparent is the fingerprinted TA505 pivot.
ucs.splunk: | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=rundll32.exe AND Processes.parent_process_name=msiexec.exe AND (Processes.parent_process="*http://*" OR Processes.parent_process="*https://*") AND (Processes.process="*\\AppData\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\ProgramData\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\Users\\Public\\*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | where user!="*$"
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let OfficeGrandparents = dynamic(["winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","wmiprvse.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName =~ "rundll32.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "msiexec.exe"                                       // parent
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://", "https://")                     // msiexec /i <remote-url> — the Get2 fetch
     or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (OfficeGrandparents)                         // or grandparent is Office
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.(dll|dat|tmp|ocx|bin|cpl)[""\s,]+\w+"   // ordinal/export named after extension
     or ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\AppData\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\Temp\")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          Grandparent       = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          MsiexecCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RundllCommandLine  = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "\\rundll32.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\msiexec.exe"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://", "https://", "/i ", "/q")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.(dll|dat|tmp|ocx|bin|cpl)[""\s,]+\w+"
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\AppData\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\Temp\")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: TA505 Get2/SDBbot Loader — rundll32 child of msiexec from user-writable path
id: 9b2e4f1a-3b5d-44a8-9e7f-ta505-get2-1
status: experimental
description: TA505 / Indrik Spider initial-access chain — weaponized Office document spawns msiexec which downloads the Get2 MSI; the MSI invokes rundll32 against a DLL staged in AppData/ProgramData/Temp/Public to load SDBbot/FlawedAmmyy/ServHelper.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0092/
  - https://blog.morphisec.com/threat-profile-evil-corp
author: SOC detection-engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1218.007
  - attack.t1218.011
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.g0092
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith: '\rundll32.exe'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\msiexec.exe'
  selection_remote_msi:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
  selection_userpath:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '\AppData\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\Users\Public\'
  filter_machine:
    User|endswith: '$'
  condition: selection_image and selection_parent and selection_remote_msi and selection_userpath and not filter_machine
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate MSI installers occasionally drop helper DLLs under ProgramData and invoke them via rundll32 — review the parent MSI URL and DLL signing context
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\\msiexec.exe OR *\\MsiExec.exe OR *\\MSIEXEC.EXE)) (@Image:(*\\rundll32.exe OR *\\Rundll32.exe OR *\\RUNDLL32.EXE)) (@ParentCommandLine:(*http\:* OR *https\:*)) (@CommandLine:(*\\AppData\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *\\Users\\Public\\*)) -@User:*\$
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\rundll32\.exe$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^msiexec\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(http://|https://)", field=ParentCommandLine)
| regex("(?i)(\\\\AppData\\\\|\\\\ProgramData\\\\|\\\\Temp\\\\|\\\\Users\\\\Public\\\\)", field=CommandLine)
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentCommandLine, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=[count(), min(@timestamp, as=FirstSeen), max(@timestamp, as=LastSeen)])
ucs.rationale: The msiexec.exe-with-remote-URL → rundll32.exe-of-DLL-in-user-writable-path chain is TA505's documented Get2/SDBbot/FlawedAmmyy delivery fingerprint (Indrik Spider, GOLD DRAKE, Manatee Tempest). Other Russian e-crime crews favour HTA, ISO, or direct PowerShell — TA505 specifically pivots through msiexec because it signs cleanly and bypasses many macro-execution policies, and SDBbot's loader is con
